For any reasonable parent, that also spanks their child, a 3 year olds tantrum is in no way punishable by a spanking. Jesus, you people seem to think that if you spank your kid that is the go to first line of punishment when in reality it should be your last recourse. 

Spanking is for repeat and grievous infractions only. A child crying is natural and part of a child's development. Most of the time it is to simply be ignored to show the child that it has no effect. 

Spanking should never be done in haste or anger. If you cannot control yourself with a child you have issues that go far beyond being a parent. My parents spanked me, it was probably the only punishment they could give me that mattered to me. My parents did spanking in a way that was appropriate, metered and effective.

I was sent to my room for my parents to have a moment to calm down, you should never spank when you are angry and never show that anger in the spanking. The waiting for the spanking was 10X worse than the spanking itself. Knowing it was coming and being unable to stop it was the worst part. 

My father would normally be charged with the spanking duty. He would sit me down and talk with me about what happened and what I had done and why I was being punished. I ofcourse tried to blubber my way out of it but he knew if I talked my way out of the punishment it would be a worthless lesson.

He would give me my pops and then it was over. I would be angry and in a huff and he would leave so I could calm down. Once I wasn't as angry any more my parents would both give me a hug/kiss and tell me they still loved me. 

This is how spanking should happen. This is a foundation for a system of punishment that is not abusive but is definitively effective. There is no need to beat your child or abuse them.

RAID 1 in theory doesn't require any calculation, just a fork so data is duplicated. If your controller is good it can also use both disks to increase read speed like a RAID 0. 

RAID 5 and 6 are both parity calculated RAIDs and require a calculation of the data bits as it writes the parity bit. This calculation can hurt performance on a RAID 5 and can get even worse on a RAID 6. 

RAID 10 is a nested raid of RAID 0 and 1. Instead of having parity it uses 50% of the space as a duplicate and the other 50% as a striped array. This gives a ~100% performance boost over a single disk with little overhead as there is no parity calculations. The downside is 2 paired drives failing still kills the array unlike a RAID 6 where 3 drives have to fail.

This has nothing to do with push vs pull its all about the fact that hot air rises... so the device blows out hot air from the bottom, it rises then that hot air gets sucked right back into the intake and the cycle repeats. This cycle over time creates a feedback loop of heat that either overheats a heavily used device or significantly reduces the life span. Flipping it face down resolves all of these issues as the hot air flows up away from the intake and the intake sucks air from the coldest part of the room.
